document.title: Host Control: let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins
document.summary: Adds Host Control end to end: the `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` client and plugin API, the `vitadeck-host-companion` CLI with built-in `core` and `systemStats` plugins that installs custom `.vdplugin` packages, SDK CLI support to build those packages with a Deck App or standalone, a LAN Listener that VitaDeck starts at boot for both Runtime Upload and links, a link store and a Shell Host Control screen, and a `host-control` example Deck App, and events the computer pushes to Deck Apps by long-polling.
document.why: Máté asked for the three Host Control slices, shaped so later Deck Apps can send keys, read sensors and set controls, act like a Stream Deck, drive several machines on different OSes, and show a T3 Code dashboard ([session](source:s5)).

sources.title: Host Control slice A: wire contract and SDK client
sources.gist: JSON-over-HTTP contract, error codes, typed registry, `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` client, shared fixtures.

sources.title: Host Control slice B: Host Companion CLI
sources.gist: Private companion package with `start` and `link`, config file, peer check, node:test suite.

sources.title: Host Control slice C: native link listener and Shell Host Control screen
sources.gist: Shared HTTP parsing, LAN address in platform, link listener and store, native getter, Shell entry and screen, C harness.

sources.label: PR #144
sources.gist: One PR for all three slices; plugins instead of a flat catalogue; several links; demo Deck App.

sources.label: T3 Code session · Oct 28
sources.gist: Implement all three issues; target use cases shape the design but are not built now; the backend extension model is left to the agent; add a demo Deck App.

sources.label: T3 Code session · Oct 29
sources.gist: Máté asked for a better host→Vita channel than polling and approved long-polling in this PR.

lookFor: [#109](source:s1) asks for flat command names and an internal `defineHostCommands`. Every request instead names a `plugin`, and `defineHostPlugin` and `command` are public, because the [session](source:s5) left the extension model open and [PR #144](source:s4) chose plugins.

[#109](source:s1) and [#111](source:s3) name the getter `nativeGetHostControlUrl()` and one stored link in `host-control-link.json`. At head `nativeGetHostControlLinks()` returns a JSON array of up to 4 links in `host-control-links.json`, keyed by a new companion `id` in the link payload, so one Deck App can reach several machines ([session](source:s5)).
[#109](source:s1) asks for a new `test:sdk` script. At head the SDK host-control tests run under the existing `test:cli` glob; no source gives a reason.
[#110](source:s2) keeps one `vita` in the companion config. At head `vitas` is an array, since several Vitas can link one companion.
[#111](source:s3) describes a `Forget link` action. At head Cross on a linked computer row forgets that one link at once.
Credentials stay deferred, as ADR 0004 says, so the built-in plugins only read information; custom plugins can act on the computer and run with the user's permissions.

Not true at head: `@vitadeck/host-companion` is still `private: true`, so a project from `create --host-plugin` or `--host-plugin-only` cannot `npm install` its companion devDependency until the package is published.

[#111](source:s3) has the Vita listen for links on 8798 only while the Shell Host Control screen is open. At head `POST /link` is a route on the LAN Listener (8787), which also serves Runtime Upload and starts at boot. After testing, Máté found the setup clunky and asked for upload and link to start together and by default ([session](source:s5)). Anyone on the LAN can now upload and link whenever VitaDeck runs.

[#110](source:s2) and [#111](source:s3) have the user run `link` again when the callback URL goes stale. At head every companion `start` relinks the Vitas it linked and never re-adds one the user forgot, as Máté asked ([session](source:s5)).

groups.title: Wire contract and SDK client
groups.why: Slice A: the contract every other piece speaks, and the client Deck Apps call ([#109](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `createHostClient` in `client.ts` turns a `defineHostPlugin` registry from `plugin.ts` into typed methods that POST the `protocol.ts` envelope and map every failure to a `HostResult`, and `watchHostEvents` keeps one `core.events` wait open per watcher; `plugin.ts` also gives authors typed `event<D>()` declarations, `implementHostPlugin` with a `start(emit)` lifecycle, `HostCommandError` and the `HostPluginManifest` contract, and `system-stats.ts` holds the built-in `systemStats` registry.
lookFor: `implementHostPlugin` and `HostCommandError` sit in the same subpath Deck Apps bundle; rolldown tree-shakes them from apps that never call them.
A throw from a `watchHostEvents` callback stops watching and fails the Deck App, like a throw from any other author callback; a `stop()` from a callback ends delivery before the next event or wait.

groups.title: Host Companion: vitadeck-host-companion, built-ins and plugin packages
groups.why: Slice B: the long-lived listener on the computer that performs the link and runs plugin commands ([#110](source:s2)), installable on its own and loading plugins from `.vdplugin` packages ([session](source:s5)).
groups.summary: `cli.ts` runs `start`, which serves `POST /command` from `server.ts` over `core`, the built-in `systemStats` and every `.vdplugin` package `plugin.ts` loads from `~/.vitadeck/plugins/` or `--plugin` (reloading them on change through `setPlugins`), `install`/`remove`, which unpack and delete those packages, and `link`, which POSTs the link payload from `link.ts` to the Vita LAN Listener (port 8787 by default) and records the Vita in `config.ts`; every `start` relinks the recorded Vitas with `relink: true`, one at a time, retrying an unanswering one every 30 s and dropping one that answers `unknown_link`; `rolldown.config.mjs` bundles it with the SDK into one dependency-free `vitadeck-host-companion` bin. `notify` sends a `core` notice, `core.events` and `core.notify` live in `core.ts`, and the server starts plugin lifecycles once the port is bound and stops them on reload or close.
lookFor: Subtle: `HostCommandError` is matched by `name` and wire `code`, not `instanceof`, because each package bundles its own copy of the class.
A package's entry is imported as `<file URL>?v=<sha256 of the entry>`, so a rebuilt entry loads fresh but a rebuild that changes only `files/` keeps the cached module; plugins read `files/` per call.

`install` stages into `.install-*` inside the plugins folder, validates, then renames to `<id>.vdplugin`; the extractor refuses several roots, backslashes, empty segments and `..`, ignores `__MACOSX/`, and keeps no file modes.
Paths resolve against `INIT_CWD` only under the repo's own `host-companion` script; elsewhere against the working directory.
On macOS `systemStats` counts free, inactive and speculative `vm_stat` pages as available; elsewhere it uses `os.freemem()`, which reads `MemAvailable` on Linux.
`core.events` answers `unknown_plugin` for a plugin the companion has not loaded, so a Deck App watching a missing plugin finds out instead of waiting forever.

A relink always targets port 8787 on the stored Vita IP, because the config keeps IPs only (they double as the answer allowlist); a Vita whose listener fell forward to another port needs `link` again.

groups.title: Events from the computer by long-polling
groups.why: Máté asked for a better host→Vita direction than polling ([session](source:s6)): events reach the Vita within one round trip while the Vita keeps making only outbound calls.
groups.summary: `events.ts` numbers each plugin's last 100 events and holds a `core.events` wait until that plugin's next one or 25 s, and `fetch.c` aborts pending fetches through curl's progress callback when a Deck App stops, which `js_limits_harness` proves with a server that never answers.
lookFor: A wait with no `after`, or an `after` ahead of the log (a companion restart), answers at once with `next` and starts watching from now; events are best effort across restarts and beyond 100 per plugin.

`fetch_shutdown` sets `cancelled` under `fetch_mutex` before joining, and the progress callback, called about once a second while curl connects or waits, returns non-zero to abort; a Deck App reload with a held wait takes about a second instead of up to 25 s.
Every idle watching Deck App costs one request at the companion, renewed every 25 s, and one native fetch thread on the Vita.

groups.title: SDK CLI: build Host Plugin packages, with or without a Deck App
groups.why: Authors keep a plugin in a Deck App's repo or on its own, and ship it as a `.vdplugin` package like the `.vdapp` ([session](source:s5)).
groups.summary: `hostPlugin: { entry, files? }` in `vitadeck.config.json` makes `build` bundle the entry into a staged `<slug>.vdplugin` folder with `manifest.json` and `files/`, swap it in and zip it, `entry` becomes optional so a plugin-only project builds and `dev`s alone, and `create --host-plugin` / `--host-plugin-only` scaffold the two layouts from the `host-plugin` and `host-plugin-only` templates.
lookFor: A failed plugin build leaves the previous `<slug>.vdplugin` in place: the package is written to `<slug>.vdplugin.tmp` and renamed over the old folder only after everything succeeds.
`vitadeck dev` takes a Runtime Upload URL exactly when the project has a Deck App `entry`; a plugin-only project rebuilds on save without one.

The standalone template takes `@vitadeck/sdk` as a peer and dev dependency and exports `./host/plugin.ts`, so a Deck App installing it from git or npm shares its own SDK; `copy-templates.ts` rewrites `workspace:*` in every template's dependency fields.
The scaffolded plugin id is the project slug, so two projects scaffolded with the same name collide on one companion.

groups.title: Shared native helpers moved out of upload and storage
groups.why: The link listener reuses Runtime Upload's request reading, the manifest's jimp parsing, and Deck App Storage's safe file replace, so [#111](source:s3) moves them where both callers reach them.
groups.summary: Upload's HTTP helpers move to `src/net/http.c`, its LAN address detection to `src/platform/lan_address_*`, jimp and JSON escaping to `src/core/json.c`, and Deck App Storage's replace-file logic to `vd_replace_file` in `src/core/util.c`.
lookFor: A Deck App Storage write that fails to move the old file aside now reports "Could not write Deck App Storage." instead of "Could not replace Deck App Storage."; the `.tmp` and `.bak` names stay the same, so a backup left by an older build is still recovered.
`http_read_request` always NUL-terminates the body it returns, so the link parser can hand it to jimp; Runtime Upload ignores the extra byte.

groups.title: LAN Listener, link store and native getter
groups.why: Slice C: VitaDeck accepts links, keeps them across restarts, and lets Deck Apps read them ([#111](source:s3)). Links share the listener with Runtime Upload and start by default, as Máté asked after testing ([session](source:s5)).
groups.summary: `src/net/lan_listener.c`, the former `src/upload/http_server.c`, adds a `POST /link` route next to `/upload` on 8787+ and `main.c` starts it at boot; `link.c` validates a link and stores up to 4 through `vd_replace_file`, and `host_control_links_relink` updates an existing link in place for a `relink: true` request or answers 404 `unknown_link`, and `nativeGetHostControlLinks` in `jslib/host_control.c` hands the list to the SDK client.
lookFor: Every client socket now gets a 15 s `SO_RCVTIMEO` per read, uploads included, so a client that goes quiet frees its handler slot; a slow but steady 16 MiB upload is unaffected.
`lan_listener_stop` shuts client sockets down while holding the listener mutex, so a handler cannot close its fd and let a Deck App `fetch` reuse that number first.
A link no longer stops the listener; a rejected or accepted link only leaves a `Link rejected: …` or `Linked to …` message for the Shell.

A relink keeps the link where it is in the list and writes the file only when the name or URL changed; only a change shows `Relinked … at …` in the Shell, so a routine companion restart is silent on the Vita.

groups.title: Shell listener toggle and Host Control screen
groups.why: The user reads the Vita address, turns the listener off when wanted, and forgets links on the Vita ([#111](source:s3), [session](source:s5)).
groups.summary: The Upload row becomes `Upload and link`, showing the LAN Listener URL and toggling it, and the Host Control row opens `VD_SHELL_HOST_CONTROL`, which shows the `link` command with the listener address and the linked computers without touching the listener.
lookFor: With no Deck App installed, `shell_show_home` focuses the Host Control row through `home_first_row()`, so the first Cross on a fresh Vita opens Host Control instead of stopping the listener.

Focus is a row index and uploads add package rows above the entries; `keep_entry_focus()` in `shell_update` shifts focus by the packages added while it sits on an entry, so an install does not slide it from Host Control onto Upload and link.
Messages from the listener (an install, a link, a rejected link) land in the Shell message even while the Shell is hidden, and show when it opens.

groups.title: host-control example Deck App
groups.why: The [session](source:s5) asked for a demo Deck App showcasing Host Control.
groups.summary: `App.tsx` polls `linkedHosts()` and each host's built-in `systemStats.read`, imported from the SDK, lists the computers with live CPU, and shows the selected one's capabilities, gauges and an Echo round trip, plus the latest `core` notice it watches with `watchHostEvents`.
lookFor: After a `timeout` the demo polls that computer every 30 s instead of every second, because the native fetch keeps running up to its 30 s curl cap after the SDK gives up at 5 s.
`HostDetails` asks for capabilities by `host.url` rather than `hostId`, so a relink to a new URL while the demo runs asks again instead of keeping the old error.

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): relink attempts run one at a time and re-read the config
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Retries for different Vitas ran on independent timers, and each save
wrote the same temporary file from a config read before the request.
All attempts now share one queue, a failure is logged, and linkVita
reads the config again just before changing its Vitas. Also list
unknown_link with the other link endpoint codes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): the companion relinks its Vitas on every start
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A new computer IP or companion port broke commands until the user ran
`link` again. `start` now re-sends the link to every Vita in its config
with `relink: true`, which VitaDeck applies only to a link it still has,
so a computer forgotten in the Shell is not linked back: VitaDeck
answers 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita
that does not answer is retried every 30 s. The host-control demo asks
for capabilities again when a relink changes the URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: refactor(shell): read the row count once when Home opens
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(shell): an install keeps Home focus on the entry row it was on
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Package rows sit above Upload and link and Host Control, and focus is a
row index, so the first upload into an empty library moved focus from
Host Control onto Upload and link, where the next Cross stopped the
listener.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(shell): an empty Shell focuses Host Control so Cross keeps listening
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
With no Deck App installed, Home opened on Upload and link, and the first
Cross stopped the listener the empty-state hint points to. Also shut down
client sockets while holding the listener lock, and fix two stale lines
in ADR 0004 and the upload script.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(shell): one LAN Listener for upload and link, on from startup
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Setting up a Deck App with a Host Control Plugin needed two Shell steps
and two addresses: start Upload for `vitadeck dev`, then open Host
Control for `link`. The upload server now also serves `POST /link`,
VitaDeck starts it at boot, and the Shell row turns it off and on. Both
CLIs take the same Vita address (port 8787).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): start plugin lifecycles after binding the port
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A busy port no longer leaves a plugin's timers running. Stopping twice is a
no-op, each plugin keeps its own 100 events, and core.events answers
unknown_plugin for a plugin the companion has not loaded. The SDK says a
throw from a watch callback stops watching.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): computers push events to Deck Apps by long-polling
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A plugin declares Host Control Events next to its commands and emits them
from a start(emit) lifecycle the companion runs while it is loaded. The
companion numbers recent events, and core.events holds a request until the
plugin's next event or 25 s. watchHostEvents in the SDK keeps one such
request open, so an event reaches the Vita within one round trip. core.notify
and `vitadeck-host-companion notify` let any script send a notice, which the
host-control demo shows.

Stopping a Deck App now cancels its pending fetches through curl's progress
callback, so a held request no longer stalls a reload or shutdown.

commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Plugins will carry more than code (scripts, data, binaries), so the single
bundled file becomes a package like the Deck App's: `vitadeck build` writes a
<slug>.vdplugin folder (manifest.json, companion.mjs, optional files/) and a
<slug>.vdplugin.zip. `hostPlugin` becomes { entry, files? }. The companion

package folders recursively.

vitadeck-host-companion bin, and js/host-plugins is gone.

commits.subject: feat(sdk): Host Control wire contract, plugins, and client
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

added: [#110](source:s2) and [#111](source:s3) have the user run `link` again when the callback URL goes stale. At head every companion `start` relinks the Vitas it linked and never re-adds one the user forgot, as Máté asked ([session](source:s5)).

groups.title: Wire contract and SDK client
Host Companion: vitadeck-host-companion, built-ins and plugin packages

summary.before: `cli.ts` runs `start`, which serves `POST /command` from `server.ts` over `core`, the built-in `systemStats` and every `.vdplugin` package `plugin.ts` loads from `~/.vitadeck/plugins/` or `--plugin` (reloading them on change through `setPlugins`), `install`/`remove`, which unpack and delete those packages, and `link`, which POSTs the link payload from `link.ts` to the Vita LAN Listener (port 8787 by default) and records the Vita in `config.ts`; `rolldown.config.mjs` bundles it with the SDK into one dependency-free `vitadeck-host-companion` bin. `notify` sends a `core` notice, `core.events` and `core.notify` live in `core.ts`, and the server starts plugin lifecycles once the port is bound and stops them on reload or close.
summary.after: `cli.ts` runs `start`, which serves `POST /command` from `server.ts` over `core`, the built-in `systemStats` and every `.vdplugin` package `plugin.ts` loads from `~/.vitadeck/plugins/` or `--plugin` (reloading them on change through `setPlugins`), `install`/`remove`, which unpack and delete those packages, and `link`, which POSTs the link payload from `link.ts` to the Vita LAN Listener (port 8787 by default) and records the Vita in `config.ts`; every `start` relinks the recorded Vitas with `relink: true`, one at a time, retrying an unanswering one every 30 s and dropping one that answers `unknown_link`; `rolldown.config.mjs` bundles it with the SDK into one dependency-free `vitadeck-host-companion` bin. `notify` sends a `core` notice, `core.events` and `core.notify` live in `core.ts`, and the server starts plugin lifecycles once the port is bound and stops them on reload or close.

added: A relink always targets port 8787 on the stored Vita IP, because the config keeps IPs only (they double as the answer allowlist); a Vita whose listener fell forward to another port needs `link` again.

groups.title: LAN Listener, link store and native getter

summary.before: `src/net/lan_listener.c`, the former `src/upload/http_server.c`, adds a `POST /link` route next to `/upload` on 8787+ and `main.c` starts it at boot; `link.c` validates a link and stores up to 4 through `vd_replace_file`, and `nativeGetHostControlLinks` in `jslib/host_control.c` hands the list to the SDK client.
summary.after: `src/net/lan_listener.c`, the former `src/upload/http_server.c`, adds a `POST /link` route next to `/upload` on 8787+ and `main.c` starts it at boot; `link.c` validates a link and stores up to 4 through `vd_replace_file`, and `host_control_links_relink` updates an existing link in place for a `relink: true` request or answers 404 `unknown_link`, and `nativeGetHostControlLinks` in `jslib/host_control.c` hands the list to the SDK client.

added: A relink keeps the link where it is in the list and writes the file only when the name or URL changed; only a change shows `Relinked … at …` in the Shell, so a routine companion restart is silent on the Vita.

groups.title: host-control example Deck App

added: `HostDetails` asks for capabilities by `host.url` rather than `hostId`, so a relink to a new URL while the demo runs asks again instead of keeping the old error.
